global.headline: Abu Dhabi signs OpenAI deals to run government services on UAE-hosted AI
global.source_title: Abu Dhabi agrees OpenAI deals to transform government services and education
global.summary: Abu Dhabi's government and OpenAI launched a Machine-Readable Government initiative, already piloted on food imports, alongside agreements with Mubadala and G42's Inception42. The deals followed a meeting between Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed and Sam Altman.
key_insights: The first pilot is live at the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, with processing on OpenAI's inference setup in UAE data centres.
Mubadala, Inception42 and OpenAI will apply AI to investment analysis, deal sourcing and risk assessment.
Inception42 and OpenAI signed a five-year agreement covering government, enterprise and education. No values were disclosed.
global.impact: Importers dealing with Abu Dhabi's food-safety authority are the first users. The setup shows governments pairing frontier models with in-country hosting.

global.headline: Linux 7.4-rc1 lands near 20,000 commits as AI-assisted patches go mainstream
global.source_title: Linux 7.4 lands with a massive flood of AI patches and record commits
global.summary: The first Linux 7.4 release candidate pulled in close to 20,000 commits, against roughly 15,000 in a typical release. Linus Torvalds said AI-generated contributions are now a normal part of kernel work, but wants them sent during the merge window rather than late in the cycle.
key_insights: Torvalds noted that AI-suggested patches often still need rewriting by developers.
He cautioned AI may not explain the whole jump, since 7.4 is expected to be the next long-term support release.
Seven or eight weekly release candidates are expected, pointing to a final release around the end of December.
global.impact: Kernel maintainers face heavier review loads, and companies shipping Linux are likely to standardise on 7.4 as their next long-term base.

global.headline: UK watchdog opens competition probe into Meta's AI content terms for publishers
global.source_title: Competition watchdog to investigate Meta terms for publishers and businesses
global.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority is examining whether Meta's updated business terms, which would let it use publishers' website content in its products and AI features without giving them a choice, breach the 1998 Competition Act. Meta has paused the change and says there are no grounds for the probe.
key_insights: The CMA will first assess whether Meta holds a dominant position in a relevant UK market.
The regulator warned the terms could amount to unfair trading conditions for thousands of UK businesses.
Meta says it has committed not to change its terms without consulting publishers and other stakeholders.
global.impact: UK news publishers gain leverage over how their content is used in AI features, and the outcome could set terms for platform use of publisher content.

global.headline: Poisoned Claude Code extension planted SSH backdoors on developer machines
global.source_title: Claude Code extension poisoned with persistent SSH backdoor
global.summary: A tampered version (2.1.313) of Anthropic's Claude Code extension was available for about 11 hours on 29 October. It added an attacker's SSH key, opened a tunnel to the attacker's server and set up persistence. Cursor says at most 5,000 users could be affected.
key_insights: The code ran as soon as the extension loaded, with no user action needed.
It reported hostnames, usernames, Git emails, public IPs and the names of key-like environment variables.
Uninstalling is not enough: check authorized keys for an entry labelled svc-telemetry and rotate credentials.
global.impact: Developers who installed it that day should treat the machine as compromised. AI coding tools are now a software supply-chain target.

global.headline: Apple Intelligence comes to China in December, powered by Alibaba's Qwen
global.source_title: Apple Brings First Apple Intelligence Features to China in iOS 27.3
global.summary: Apple said its first Apple Intelligence features for users in China open for developer testing on 4 November and launch with iOS 27.3 in December. Alibaba's Qwen powers Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence there; the next-generation Siri AI shown at WWDC 2026 is not included.
key_insights: Features include Live Translation, Writing Tools, notification summaries, Photos Clean Up and Genmoji.
Supported iPhones include iPhone 15 Pro models, iPhone 16 and later and iPhone Air, set to English or Simplified Chinese.
Other Apple platforms follow once the necessary approvals are obtained.
global.impact: iPhone owners in China get Apple's AI features for the first time, delivered through a local model partner, with other devices waiting on approval.

india.headline: TRAI draft would make telcos answerable for every AI system they use
india.source_title: TRAI draft AI guidelines hold telcos accountable for vendor AI
india.summary: TRAI's draft guidelines on responsible AI in telecom, released on 30 October, would hold operators accountable for the outcomes of all AI systems they run, whether built in-house or bought from vendors. Comments are open until 27 November.
key_insights: Operators would need a board-approved AI policy, reviewed yearly and filed with TRAI, plus risk ratings and an inventory of systems.
Every system would need pre-launch testing and human oversight; the two most serious of four incident levels must be reported.
Each operator would need a senior-led AI Governance and Safety Committee.
india.impact: India's mobile operators would carry liability for vendor-built AI, pushing suppliers of customer-service bots and network tools toward audit-ready systems.

india.headline: Vultr switches on 20 MW AMD GPU supercluster in Chennai
india.source_title: Vultr Chennai AI Supercluster: 20 MW, 10,000 AMD GPUs
india.summary: Cloud provider Vultr has launched a 20 MW AI supercluster in Chennai with about 10,000 AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs in its first phase, its largest AI deployment in India. Tamil Nadu has enabled 150 MW of connected power for the site.
key_insights: A 2027 expansion is planned on AMD MI455X GPUs and the Helios rack-scale design.
Vultr targets 600 MW of AI capacity in India by 2028 and gigawatt scale by 2029, without firm timelines.
Supermicro is named as the server partner.
india.impact: Indian startups and enterprises gain another large pool of in-country GPU capacity, and Tamil Nadu adds to its data-centre pipeline.

india.headline: Rhodium: India's subsidised GPUs run near 20% use; its AI edge is services
india.source_title: India Has $300 Billion in Data Centre Pledges but GPUs at 20% Use; Its Real AI Edge Is Services, Says Rhodium Group
india.summary: A Rhodium Group report finds GPUs subsidised under the IndiaAI Mission running at about 20% utilisation, with most domestic enterprise AI work on global clouds. It argues India's real AI opportunity lies in IT services rather than data-centre build-out.
key_insights: Yotta is estimated to earn about 80% of its revenue from overseas customers.
AI services are roughly 7.5% of TCS revenue and 8% of Infosys revenue, per the report.
The case for Indic-language models is sound, it says, but the home market may be too small to fund frontier models alone.
india.impact: The findings question state incentive races and job claims for data centres, and point policy toward demand and services over more subsidised capacity.

india.headline: Bihar cabinet approves AI Policy 2026 with subsidies for startups and GCCs
india.source_title: Bihar AI Policy 2026: State Cabinet Approves Plan to Boost AI Innovation, Startups, Investment
india.summary: Bihar's cabinet, under Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, approved the Bihar AI Policy 2026 to attract AI companies, startups and global capability centres. It offers subsidies on capital spending, interest, cloud computing, rent and electricity, plus employment-linked incentives and SGST reimbursement.
key_insights: The report gives no budget figure or numerical targets for the policy.
IT Minister Nitish Mishra framed it around innovation, investment and startups.
india.impact: Bihar joins the states competing for AI investment with cost subsidies; without published targets, its effect will be hard to measure.

india.headline: Simplismart's $14M Series B with NVIDIA leads this week's Indian AI deals
india.source_title: From Cent to Matiks — Indian Startups Raised Over $132 Mn This Week
india.summary: Indian startups raised $130.2 million between 26 and 30 October, down 29.2% from the previous week. AI infrastructure company Simplismart led the AI deals with a $14 million Series B from Dallas Venture Capital, with NVIDIA and Accel taking part.
key_insights: Live2.ai raised $13.7 million in a Pre-Series B round from IvyCap Ventures.
QwikBuild raised $2.3 million pre-seed led by Globalway, with Blume Ventures participating.
Inc42's headline says over $132M while its body gives $130.2M; JARVIS uses the body figure.
india.impact: Investors are still backing Indian AI infrastructure and application startups even as overall weekly funding fell.
